$comment: The plate corpus for the published manual (ADR-0008). Checked and rendered to a prompt sheet by scripts/art-verify.mjs. Every plate depicts an observable attribute or a rules situation; none depicts a named figure as the exemplar of a class.

style.medium: hand-inked technical illustration with a flat wash, in the manner of a printed field guide
style.palette: warm ochre, terracotta and sepia on unbleached paper; one cool grey for shadow; a single saturated gold reserved for the Star
style.light: one soft source from the upper left, consistent across every plate
style.subject_matter: painted ceramic and terracotta figurines standing on a table — the figurines are the subject and are rendered as objects, with visible glaze, chips, worn gilding and brush marks
style.background: pale unbleached paper, empty except where a plate calls for terrain
style.framing: eye level with the tabletop, so figures are seen as a player sees them

negative: living people, or figures rendered as flesh rather than as painted ceramic
text, lettering, numerals, captions, logos, watermarks or signatures inside the image
faces rendered with portrait specificity; features are suggested by paint, as on a real figurine
named or recognisable religious figure presented as the exemplar of anything
violence of any kind, weapons in use, or figures depicted as struck, falling, injured or dead
infant figure depicted other than static and unattended in a manger
reference to any publisher, game, artist or product as a style source
heraldry, skull motifs, gothic ornament or border furniture from any existing game
photorealism, 3D renders, or digital painting gloss

plates.title: The set, at eye level
plates.subject: a mixed household nativity set of perhaps fifteen figurines, plainly of different sizes, ages and paint qualities, standing scattered on a bare table
plates.composition: wide, low, slightly off-centre; the Star hangs above and to the right, the only saturated gold in the image; several figures face it, several do not
plates.caption: You have owned an army since childhood. It has simply been standing still.

plates.title: One figure-height
plates.subject: a single standing adult figurine beside a strip of card cut to exactly its height, the card marked at its midpoint with a pencil line
plates.composition: flat side-on elevation, the card laid vertically against the figure; a second copy of the card lies horizontally below, showing it in use as a measure
plates.caption: The strip is the only tape measure this game uses.

plates.title: When the set does not agree with itself
plates.subject: eight standing figurines in a row, five clearly one size and three clearly larger, the card strip held against one of the five
plates.composition: even row, side-on, the five matching figures grouped so their shared height reads instantly
plates.caption: The most numerous figure sets H, even when it is not the largest.

plates.title: Astride is a silhouette, not a story
plates.subject: three unrelated figurines that are each astride an animal — one on a camel, one on a donkey, one on a horse — differing entirely in size, dress and paint quality
plates.composition: three-quarter view, evenly spaced, all at the same scale relative to the frame so the shared outline is the only thing they have in common
plates.caption: All of these are mounted. What they carry, and who they are, does not come into it.

plates.title: A long stick with no blade
plates.subject: four figurines each holding a long straight or hooked pole — a crook, a plain staff, a walking pole, a shepherd's stick — two standing, one kneeling, one leaning
plates.composition: flat side-on, poles all rendered at the same angle so the eye reads the shared shape before the figures
plates.caption: The pole decides the class. The pose does not.

plates.title: Anything carried is a load
plates.subject: five figurines carrying wildly different things — a water jar, a basket of bread, a sheaf, a small chest, a stringed instrument — no two alike in size or dress
plates.composition: a shallow arc, each load held at a different height, so the variety is obvious and the shared attribute still reads
plates.caption: A jar and a chest are the same attribute.

plates.title: The Infant
plates.subject: a single small swaddled figurine lying in a straw manger, alone, no other figure present
plates.composition: close, centred, entirely static; the manger occupies the lower two thirds, empty pale paper above
plates.caption: It never moves, and nothing in this game can take it off the table.

plates.title: All of these are Heralds
plates.subject: three winged figurines of visibly different make — one tall and slender, one squat and folk-carved, one with gilt flaking off the wing edges
plates.composition: three-quarter view, wings the dominant shape in all three silhouettes, feet at different heights to suggest they are not bound by the ground
plates.caption: Wings, and nothing else, make a Herald.

plates.title: All of these are Beasts of Burden
plates.subject: three four-legged animal figurines standing at least half a figure-height at the shoulder — an ox, a donkey, a camel — with a standing human figurine behind for scale
plates.composition: side-on elevation in a row, the human figure at the far right, a faint pencil line across all four at the shoulder height that decides the class
plates.caption: Shoulder height decides it, not species.

plates.title: All of these are Herd Animals
plates.subject: five small four-legged figurines — sheep of three different makes, a goat, a dog — clustered close together
plates.composition: a tight huddle seen slightly from above, one animal facing outward from the group
plates.caption: Small and four-legged. They move together, whether or not you want them to.

plates.title: All of these are Riders
plates.subject: three mounted figurines, one plainly armed with a spear across the saddle, two plainly not
plates.composition: three-quarter view in a shallow line, the armed one in the middle so the eye asks the question the caption answers
plates.caption: A mounted figure carrying a weapon is still a Rider. Speed outranks the spear.

plates.title: All of these are Soldiers
plates.subject: three figurines carrying weapons or wearing armour — a helmet and shield, a spear held upright at rest, greaves and a sheathed sword — every one of them standing at ease and at rest
plates.composition: flat side-on, evenly spaced, weapons held vertically and still
plates.caption: Armour or a weapon, worn or carried. Not used.

plates.title: All of these are Drovers
plates.subject: three figurines with staffs or crooks — one standing, one kneeling with the crook still in hand, one walking — with two small animal figurines nearby
plates.composition: loose triangle, the kneeling figure at the front so the caption's point lands
plates.caption: A kneeling figure with a crook is a Drover. The crook is a rule; the knees are a pose.

plates.title: All of these are Supplicants
plates.subject: four figurines kneeling, seated on the ground or prostrate, hands empty and carrying nothing at all
plates.composition: seen slightly from above so the low posture reads clearly; a deliberate gap of empty paper where a carried object would be
plates.caption: Kneeling, and holding nothing. The empty hands are the test.

plates.title: All of these are Bearers
plates.subject: four figurines carrying loads, two standing and two kneeling with the load still in their hands
plates.composition: a row alternating standing and kneeling, so the shared load is the constant and the pose is the variable
plates.caption: A kneeling figure offering something is a Bearer, not a Supplicant. What is held outranks how it stands.

plates.title: All of these are Townsfolk
plates.subject: six figurines with nothing in common — a fisherman, a woman at a washboard, a child, a baker, a man simply standing, a figure whose occupation is unguessable
plates.composition: scattered, facing different directions, none interacting, the composition deliberately without a focal point
plates.caption: Everything the procedure did not catch. Most sets are mostly this.

plates.title: The light decides where the game is
plates.subject: a small terrain feature — a well — lit in saturated gold, with four figurines around it, and a second unlit feature to the side already going dark
plates.composition: the gold confined entirely to the well and the ground within a short radius; everything outside it in flat sepia
plates.caption: Standing where you score is standing where you are seen.

plates.title: Open, Rough, Difficult
plates.subject: one strip of table crossing three grounds in sequence — bare plaza, then straw and moss, then a stream with a low wall — with one figurine standing in each
plates.composition: a long horizontal band read left to right, the three grounds separated by their texture alone, no dividing lines
plates.caption: The display you own is the terrain chart.

plates.title: Shaken, and still on the table
plates.subject: one figurine turned away from the others with a small marker of coloured putty at its base, three other figurines nearby continuing about their business
plates.composition: the turned figure at the near right, the group receding to the left; nothing dramatic, nothing knocked over
plates.caption: Fear turns a figure around. It never takes one away.

plates.title: The road, and who chooses it
plates.subject: six terrain features laid in a rough chain across a table with the stable at one end, the Star hovering over the third, small arrows of light suggesting the two features it could move to next
plates.composition: seen from high and at an angle, the whole chain legible at once; the gold used only for the Star and the two possible next positions
plates.caption: It advances every round. The player who is losing decides which way.

plates.title: A delivered Gift is a fact
plates.subject: a figurine setting a small chest down on the straw of the stable floor beside a marker, with the manger visible at the edge of frame
plates.composition: close and low, the chest and the hands the centre of the frame, the figure's face out of shot
plates.caption: Set down, it cannot be taken back. Neither can the round you spent walking there.
